applications.name: openssh
applications.purpose: The remote authenticated SSH service the attacker brute-forces (T1110.001) and pivots through (T1021.004). A FREE, analyst-authored implementation choice: the corpus pins only that a remote authenticated service must exist, not which SSH server realises it. The non-uniqueness witness substitutes it (OpenSSH <-> Dropbear) and executes both to completion under one corpus fingerprint.

composition.notes: Pivot target realism: weak SSH credential + listening port 22 on the per-run private Docker network.

applications.name: apache_httpd
applications.purpose: The edge HTTP service whose Basic Auth realm the attacker brute-forces (T1110.001) and authenticates to (T1078) before exfiltrating the protected secret (T1005). A FREE, analyst-authored implementation choice: the corpus pins only that an edge HTTP service must exist, not which web server realises it. The non-uniqueness witness substitutes it (Apache <-> Nginx) and executes both to completion under one corpus fingerprint.

composition.notes: Web target realism: HTTP Basic Auth realm with a pre-staged weak credential and a protected secret on the per-run private network.

sut_profile.notes: Two-host edge-HTTP witness. Lab pre-stages a weak HTTP Basic Auth credential on the web target; the attacker discovers it via T1110.001 and exfiltrates the protected secret.
